args: In c-blosc2/blosc/frame.c, analyze frame_get_lazychunk() for an in-memory contiguous frame. What exact boundary and integer-overflow checks should be made before forming frame->cframe + header_len + offset, reading BLOSC2_CHUNK_CBYTES, and returning that claimed chunk size? Note any relevant constants and expected error codes, and whether frame->len or parsed frame_len should be authoritative.

The supplied ASan crash occurs because frame_get_lazychunk at c-blosc2/blosc/frame.c:1972 forms an embedded chunk pointer and reads its cbytes field, then returns the attacker-declared cbytes to frame_decompress_chunk and blosc2_decompress_ctx. The compressed-offset entry reaches a chunk header, but the claimed chunk extent exceeds the actual in-memory frame. get_coffset only checks offset > frame->len and ignores header_len addition. I am considering subtraction-based checks against frame->len: validate header_len and offset, ensure enough bytes remain to read the minimum/header cbytes field, decode cbytes, and ensure it is no larger than the remaining bytes. I want this rooted at the in-memory lazychunk branch while preserving disk/sparse frame behavior.
